title: THE ORACLE REFUSES TO DEFINE OPENING BALANCES ONCE ANY JOURNAL ENTRY HAS BEEN POSTED. OB-01 sent POST /journalentries?command=defineOpeningBalance to tenant `gerege`, where financial-activity type 300 maps to GL 15 and 26 non-contra transaction ids exist, and the oracle returned HTTP 403 with error.msg.journalentry.defining.openingbalance.not.allowed. The refusal is thrown at JournalEntryWritePlatformServiceJpaRepositoryImpl.java:717 -> :810-816, BEFORE the office lookup at :719, BEFORE validateBusinessRulesForJournalEntries at :724 and BEFORE the first write at :726-733 -- which is what made this the one opening-balance refusal capturable with no mutation, no closure and no dependence on the business date.
_note: WHAT THIS VECTOR GRADES: that the port implements the guard at :717 AT ALL, and that it places it AHEAD of the balance rule. THE PRECONDITION IS AN INPUT, NOT AMBIENT STATE, and that is T289's date strategy (c) applied to a state precondition: T289 established that a refusal whose precondition lives in the oracle 'will silently stop testing what it claims', rejected pinning the oracle and rejected recomputing the input at run time, and required the precondition to be lifted into the vector. So request.command carries the wire's ?command= value, request.contra_gl_account_id carries the financial-activity-300 mapping the oracle resolved at :708-709, and request.posted_non_contra_transaction_ids carries findNonContraTransactionIds' own answer, transcribed from errors[0].args of the captured body. The port reads a length; :812 reads CollectionUtils.isEmpty. THE ORDERING IS OBSERVED, NOT CHOSEN, AND THAT IS THE PART TO READ TWICE: OB-01's request body is UNBALANCED BY EXACTLY ONE MINOR UNIT (debit 250000.25, credit 250000.24), so the oracle had TWO independent grounds to refuse it, and it returned THIS one. Source agrees -- :717 runs before :724, and the balance check is inside :724 at :651 checkDebitAndCreditAmounts -- but here the capture settles it rather than the source. The imbalance is also the WRITE-FENCE: P-92 ('a probe whose safety comes from an EXTERNAL PRECONDITION rather than from its own content is a loaded weapon, and the danger is highest immediately after the capture SUCCEEDS'), so this probe's body is unpostable on its own content, permanently and independently of clock or tenant state. WHAT THIS VECTOR DOES NOT GRADE, stated rather than left to be assumed: errors[0].args is NOT graded. It carries all 26 transaction ids and is therefore tenant-state-dependent -- the schema's Refusal shape has three cells (status, code, message) and no fourth, and adding one would make this vector go red on any posting to this tenant that touched no journal entry of ours. The ids are carried as an INPUT instead, where their job is to be the predicate's subject and not an expectation. parameterName ('id') and the STRING-typed httpStatusCode ('403' as characters while the HTTP status is numeric) are likewise observed and ungraded; T289 item 3 pins them for the port and this schema has no slot for either. NO OTHER OPENING-BALANCE OR CLOSURE SHAPE IS OBSERVED BY THIS VECTOR: the pre-closure refusal and the future-dated refusal remain uncaptured in the promoted store, and nothing here grades them. NO LEGS AND NO TOTALS ARE ASSERTED -- the request was refused, so no entry exists and no amount was observed; the two amount_major_text tokens in request.legs are the CALLER'S OWN characters from the committed .req wire bytes and are graded by nothing. NO BALANCE IS GRADED. acc_gl_journal_entry carries office_running_balance and organization_running_balance and GATE G-12 IS OPEN on exactly them: A2-29 MEASURED them to be a SECOND SOURCE OF TRUTH rather than a cache -- made to disagree with the derived sum by MNT 2,000,000.00 on the live oracle, surviving four organisation-wide recomputes, propagating into a freshly computed row because the recompute seeds from its own prior output, and served at the contract boundary flagged runningBalanceComputed: true. This vector's schema has NO FIELD for either column. Balances are DERIVED, never written, and never read back.

provenance.rerun_invariant: THIS REFUSAL HOLDS WHILE NON-CONTRA JOURNAL ENTRIES EXIST ON THE TENANT. Re-sending OB-01's body to POST /journalentries?command=defineOpeningBalance must return HTTP 403 carrying error.msg.journalentry.defining.openingbalance.not.allowed for as long as findNonContraTransactionIds(contraId) -- the JPQL at JournalEntryRepository.java:32-34, with contraId the GL account the financial-activity type 300 mapping resolves to -- returns a non-empty list. WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS VECTOR FALSE: an EMPTY ledger, or one in which every remaining transaction id also touches the contra account, so that :812 CollectionUtils.isEmpty is true and :810-816 no longer throws. A tenant reset, a fresh tenant, or a re-pointing of financial-activity type 300 at an account every transaction touches would each do it. THE ANSWER IN THAT CASE IS RE-CAPTURE, NOT EXEMPTION: this schema admits no invariant_exemptions at all, and a refusal that has stopped refusing is a stale observation, not an excused one. Note also the SECOND, WEAKER re-run property, recorded because it is what makes re-running safe rather than what makes the vector true: OB-01's body is unbalanced by one minor unit, so even on an empty ledger it is refused (checkDebitAndCreditAmounts, :651 via :724) and writes nothing -- with a DIFFERENT code, which is precisely the falsification above and not an escape from it. .softhouse/capture/t294-openingbalance-refusal/guard-precondition.sh measures both fences and fails closed.
provenance.citation: T294. HTTP status 403 read from out/OB-01-openingbalance-after-posted-entries.status; code and message read from errors[0] of the captured response body (userMessageGlobalisationCode and defaultUserMessage, which are byte-identical to developerMessage on this error). THE WIRE MESSAGE AND THE SOURCE STRING AT :814 AGREE CHARACTER FOR CHARACTER -- there was no conflict to resolve, and had there been one the wire would have won. request.legs' amount tokens and office_id read from the committed .req wire-bytes artefact. request.contra_gl_account_id read from acc_gl_financial_activity_account (M-01/M-04, financial_activity_type 300 -> gl_account_id 15) and cross-checked against the source's own derivation at :708-709. request.posted_non_contra_transaction_ids transcribed from errors[0].args[0].value of the captured body, in wire order; its cardinality 26 agrees with the independent SQL translation of JournalEntryRepository.java:32-34 in M-01 (non_contra_transaction_id_count) and with the distinct-transaction-id census in M-02. The chart rows in request.accounts are DATA (DEC-2 §4.5), transcribed from the live acc_gl_account read recorded in the handoff.

refusal.message: Defining Opening balances not allowed after journal entries posted

graded_against.note: A port that implements defineOpeningBalance as a seeding operation and never reaches validateJournalEntriesArePostedBefore (:717) falls through to the balance rule and returns error.msg.glJournalEntry.invalid.mismatch.debits.credits -- the RIGHT STATUS for the WRONG REASON. refusal.http_status is deliberately NOT claimed here: both refusals are 403, and T9-F1b forbids recording a kill on a cell that does not diverge. The code and the message are the cells that tell one 403 from another, and this vector kills on exactly those two.
